categories.title: US–Israel–Iran
categories.contest: Whether a campaign of strikes is a policy with an end, or a war nobody has named.

beginnings.line: Congress overrode President Nixon's veto and enacted the War Powers Resolution, requiring presidents to consult Congress and report within 48 hours of sending forces into hostilities.
beginnings.how: This is the statute under which Trump's war reports, the 60-day clock dispute and the 2026 votes in Congress on ending the Iran war were all argued.

object.quote: It is the purpose of this chapter to fulfill the intent of the framers of the Constitution of the United States and insure that the collective judgment of both the Congress and the President will apply to the introduction of United States Armed Forces into hostilities, or into situations where imminent involvement in hostilities is clearly indicated by the circumstances, and to the continued use of such forces in hostilities or in such situations.

beginnings.line: Ukraine, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States signed the Budapest Memorandum, in which Russia pledged to respect Ukraine's existing borders after Ukraine gave up its nuclear weapons.

categories.title: Climate
categories.contest: Whether long-term planetary risk warrants remaking how the country makes energy, or whether the remaking costs more than the risk.

beginnings.line: Congress and President Nixon enacted the Clean Air Amendments of 1970, directing the new EPA to set standards for any air pollutant from new motor vehicles that endangers public health or welfare.
beginnings.how: Its Section 202 language became the statutory hook for federal greenhouse gas rules, and the later fight over whether that law displaces or preempts state suits is the core question in Boulder's case.

categories.title: Power
categories.contest: Whether institutions should constrain elected power even when that means overruling what voters chose.

beginnings.line: The Constitutional Convention signed the Constitution, whose Article I, Section 6 shields members of Congress from being questioned elsewhere for legislative speech or debate and limits arrest during sessions.
beginnings.how: It sets the constitutional baseline for how far the executive branch may go in investigating a sitting member of Congress such as Rep. Omar.

object.title: The Constitution of the United States
object.quote: They shall in all Cases, except Treason, Felony and Breach of the Peace, be privileged from Arrest during their Attendance at the Session of their respective Houses, and in going to and returning from the same; and for any Speech or Debate in either House, they shall not be questioned in any other Place.
object.check_note: in the Object Matrix; its link is checked by check_links.py

beginnings.line: The Supreme Court in Gravel v. United States held the Speech or Debate Clause protects legislative acts of members and aides from executive prosecution, but not conduct outside the legislative process.
beginnings.how: It defines what the Justice Department may and may not pursue against a member of Congress, which frames any dispute over the Omar investigation.

categories.title: Outbreak secrecy
categories.contest: Whether a state that withholds or contradicts information during a suspected outbreak protects its public from panic, or endangers it by delaying the trust and cooperation containment depends on.

beginnings.line: The Soviet Union, the United States and the United Kingdom opened the Biological Weapons Convention for signature, with Article V obliging parties to consult and cooperate in solving problems under the treaty.
beginnings.how: Article V is the treaty channel through which Washington's pressure on Moscow over a lab death at a plague institute could be framed.

categories.stakes: The question is whether AI companies should answer for the injuries their products cause, or whether the gains justify leaving patients and the public to absorb some of the damage. State legislatures, regulators, and executives are settling it now, in who gets to deploy AI and who is held liable.

categories.title: Infrastructure cyberattacks
categories.contest: Whether firms that run critical systems for many customers should be held responsible for attacks through their networks, or whether the victims and attackers alone should bear the loss.

beginnings.line: The NotPetya malware spread worldwide through a poisoned update to the M.E.Doc accounting software, and US agencies were notified of infections across multiple countries and sectors, including Germany and France.
beginnings.how: It is an early case of one vendor's update channel carrying damage to many customers who never dealt with the attacker, the pattern behind the Danfoss attack.

beginnings.line: President Joe Biden signed Executive Order 14028, directing agencies to raise software supply chain security and requiring service providers to share incident and threat information that could affect government networks.
beginnings.how: It shows a government placing duties on suppliers rather than leaving all risk with customers, one side of the question of who answers for a vendor link.

beginnings.line: The REvil group used a flaw in Kaseya's VSA remote management software to push ransomware to managed service providers and their downstream customers, and Kaseya told customers to shut down their servers.
beginnings.how: Kaseya is a close precedent for Danfoss: one vendor's control layer let attackers reach many customers at once, with losses landing on the customers.

object.quote: On July 2, 2021, Kaseya shut down their SaaS servers and recommended Kaseya VSA customers shutdown their on-premises VSA servers.

beginnings.line: The European Parliament and the Council adopted the NIS 2 Directive, extending mandatory cybersecurity duties to more sectors and requiring Member States to supervise covered entities, including those serving other firms.
beginnings.how: France and Germany must apply this EU framework, which sets the legal baseline for what a supplier of critical systems owes its customers.

object.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS 2 Directive)
object.author: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
object.quote: Trust service providers should be required to take all appropriate and proportionate measures to manage the risks posed to their services, including in relation to customers and relying third parties, and to report incidents under this Directive.

beginnings.line: France's national computer emergency response team, CERT-FR, issued alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 on numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC refrigeration controllers, advising operators to disconnect them or filter access.
beginnings.how: It is the first official French statement on the supermarket attack, and it treats an internet-exposed management interface as contrary to good practice, which bears on who carries the blame.

categories.stakes: When hackers reach many customers through one provider's network, the law has not settled whether the provider answers for the damage or whether the loss stays with the attacked store and the criminal who cannot be found. Courts, insurers, and legislators must decide who pays, and when, and who gains from the answer.
